'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[United States and the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[President of the United States]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that the [[United States]] [[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|will send]] 31 [[M1 Abrams]] [[Main battle tank|main battle tanks]] to [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/01/25/ukraine-war-news-us-will-send-abrams-tanks.html (CNBC)]
*[[Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria]]
**Forty people are killed by an [[airstrike]] against [[Fula people|Fulani people]] in Rukubi, [[Nasarawa State]], [[Nigeria]]. The [[massacre]] is blamed on the [[Nigerian Army|army]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2023/01/27/herders-blame-airstrike-that-killed-dozens-on-nigerias-air-force/ (Africa News)]
*[[2022–2023 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions]]
**A [[Air Force of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|DRC Air Force]] [[Sukhoi Su-25]] is hit by [[Anti-aircraft warfare|anti-aircraft fire]] over the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda border|Rwandan border]]. The [[Politics of Rwanda|Rwandan government]] says that its [[Rwanda Defence Force|forces]] took "defensive measures" against a plane that had "violated its airspace". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-64397725 (BBC News)]
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
**[[France]] agrees to withdraw its 400 [[Special Operations Command (France)|special forces]] personnel from [[Burkina Faso]], following Saturday's mandate from the [[Patriotic Movement for Safeguard and Restoration|ruling military junta]] that France withdraw within one month. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-64397730 (BBC News)]
*[[Algeciras church attacks]]
**One person is killed and four others are injured when a man wielding a [[machete]] breaks into two [[church (building)|churches]] in [[Algeciras]], [[Andalusia]], [[Spain]]. A 25-year-old [[Moroccans in Spain|Moroccan]] man is arrested. [https://www.elmundo.es/andalucia/2023/01/25/63d1825621efa015088b457b.html (''El Mundo'')]
*Twelve people are injured when a bomb [[explode]]s in a market in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo| Beni]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], [https://apnews.com/article/islamic-state-group-politics-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-assault-united-nations-3966e88e590b9101aacc999180d13120 (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[UNESCO]] places the ruins of the [[Sabaeans|Kingdom of Saba]] in modern-day [[Yemen]], the historic center of [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]], and the [[Rashid Karami|Rachid Karameh]] International Fair in [[Tripoli, Lebanon|Tripoli]], [[Lebanon]], on its [[List of World Heritage in Danger|list of World Heritage Sites in Danger]]. UNESCO cites [[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|ongoing]] [[Russo-Ukrainian War|conflicts]] and lack of funding due to the [[Lebanese liquidity crisis]] as the reasons for their inclusion. [https://www.npr.org/2023/01/25/1151330239/odesa-world-heritage-in-danger-yemen-lebanon-unesco (NPR)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021–2023 inflation surge]]
**The [[Bank of Canada]] raises its benchmark [[interest rate]] to 4.5 percent, the highest since the [[2007–2008 financial crisis]], amid high levels of [[inflation]] and vacancies affecting the [[Economy of Canada|Canadian economy]]. [https://financialpost.com/news/economy/bank-of-canada-interest-rate-decision-2023 (''Financial Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[Hong Kong]]-registered [[ship]] carrying 22 people [[capsize]]s off the coast of [[Japan]]. Eight crew members are dead, 13 are rescued and two others still missing. [https://www.barrons.com/news/8-dead-including-6-chinese-nationals-after-ship-sinks-near-japan-china-s-state-media-01674717307 (''AFP via Barron's'')]
*A [[Philippine Air Force]] [[SIAI-Marchetti SF.260|SF.260]] [[training flight]] from [[Sangley Point Airport]] in [[Cavite City]], [[Philippines]], [[Plane crash|crashes]] into a [[paddy field]] in [[Pilar, Bataan|Pilar]], [[Bataan]], killing two people on board. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/military-plane-crash-pilar-bataan-january-25-2023/ (''Rappler'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[NK News]] reports that the [[North Korean government]] has imposed a five-day [[lockdown]] in [[Pyongyang]] due to the spread of an unspecified [[respiratory infection]]. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/01/25/23/n-korea-locks-down-capital-over-respiratory-illness (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran and weapons of mass destruction]]
**[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
***[[International Atomic Energy Agency]] Director General [[Rafael Grossi]] says that [[Iran]] has now amassed enough material for "several [[nuclear weapon]]s", and calls for new diplomatic efforts in order to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear bomb. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/01/25/middleeast/iran-nuclear-weapons-iaea-chief-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Iran–European Union relations]], [[Iran–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[Iran]] places sanctions on more than 30 [[United Kingdom|UK]] and [[European Union|EU]]-affiliated individuals in a tit-for-tat response to a new round of sanctions by the European Union over the [[Mahsa Amini protests]]. Sanctioned individuals include [[Attorney General for England and Wales|UK Attorney General]] [[Victoria Prentis]], [[Chief of the General Staff (United Kingdom)|UK Army Chief of Staff]] [[Patrick Sanders (British Army officer)|Sir Patrick Sanders]], and three staff members of ''[[Charlie Hebdo]]''. [https://www.rferl.org/a/iran-sanctions-europeans-tit-tat-protests/32239614.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Brokstedt stabbing]]
**Two people are killed and seven others are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] on a [[passenger train]] in [[Brokstedt]], [[Steinburg]], [[Schleswig-Holstein]], [[Germany]]. [https://itv.com/news/2023-01-25/two-dead-and-five-injured-after-man-stabs-passengers-on-german-train (ITV)]
*[[Human rights in Russia]]
**The [[Moscow City Court]] orders the closure of the [[Moscow Helsinki Group]], [[Russia]]'s oldest [[human rights]] organization. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-helsinki-group-closed/32239220.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 New Zealand Labour Party leadership election]]
**[[Leader of the New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party leader]] [[Chris Hipkins]] is sworn in as the 41st [[prime minister of New Zealand]] by [[Governor-General of New Zealand|Governor-General]] [[Cindy Kiro]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20230124-jacinda-ardern-replaced-as-new-zealand-pm-at-official-ceremony (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Cabinet of Borjana Krišto]]
**The [[Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Parliamentary Assembly]] of [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] votes 23–21 to approve the new [[Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Council of Ministers]] to be led by [[Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina|ethnic Croat]] former [[President of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Federation President]] [[Borjana Krišto]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/bosnia-kristo-governing-council-vote/32239575.html (RFE/RL)]
